doc: The one place the rule is not an exact ceil: radii (inputs.radius_km, texel 3, cap 1 << 20) whose w = 2 pi radius / texel is exactly ONE ULP above 2^5, 2^8, 2^10, 2^12 and 2^14. math.log2 returns the integer itself (the true value is 0.2 to 0.4 ulp above it and rounds back), so ceil gives k and the Python width is 2^k (32, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384), where the exact rule would give 2^(k+1) (64, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768; params.exact_rule_width, informational: NOT the expected output). The oracle follows math.log2: a port must call its libm log2 on w and take the ceil, not test w against a power of two in integers. This relies on log2 being correctly rounded here (error below 0.5 ulp, which the Python platform libm gives); a log2 with up to 1 ulp of error may return the next double and then agrees with the exact rule instead, so these rows are the behavior of the oracle, not a portable truth. Integers: exact.
